evals.name: bare-walls-no-materials
evals.prompt: I opened my Iraqi house model in Revit and the walls look empty in section — they have no material and no plaster layers, just a single block of 'Structure'. Can you set up proper wall types and fix this?
evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes the bare single-layer / no-material defect, runs validate first to confirm, then creates the Iraqi multi-layer wall catalog (cement plaster -> thermostone/block core -> gypsum plaster) with real materials, and re-validates to PASS. Must NOT touch mohammad.rvt / Vilaa.0001.rvt if those are the active doc.
assertions: Inspects the active document's wall types before changing anything (baseline)
Creates multi-layer wall types with at least 3 layers and assigned materials (plaster/core/plaster)
Wall type names follow the 'Iraqi ...' convention (e.g. 'Iraqi Exterior Wall - 25cm')
Refuses to write to mohammad.rvt or Vilaa.0001.rvt if either is the active reference document
Re-runs the wall-standard validator after the fix and reports PASS/FAIL

evals.name: audit-wall-thicknesses
evals.prompt: Before I send this Revit model for documentation, can you audit the walls and tell me which ones don't meet the Iraqi standard thicknesses? Don't change anything yet, just flag problems.
evals.expected_output: Skill runs ONLY the read-only validate_wall_standards routine, names each offending used wall type, and flags non-standard thicknesses (not in {120,200,250,360}mm), bare walls, and cryptic names. Makes no model changes.
assertions: Runs a read-only validation and makes no transaction / no model change
Names each non-conforming wall type with its thickness and instance count
Flags thicknesses outside the standard set {120,200,250,360} mm

evals.name: standardize-cryptic-types
evals.prompt: My villa model's wall types are named things like '25', '0.1', 'b' and '25 2' — total mess. I want them brought up to our Iraqi BIM standard with proper layers and clean names. Walk me through it.
evals.expected_output: Skill explains the workflow (validate -> create catalog -> remap -> join -> re-validate), creates the named multi-layer catalog, prints a thickness-based remap suggestion mapping old cryptic types to standard ones, and keeps wall reassignment as an explicit user-confirmed step.
assertions: Explains the ordered workflow (baseline validate, create catalog, remap, joins, re-validate)
Creates the multi-layer named catalog with materials
Produces a remap suggestion mapping cryptic types to standard ones by thickness
Treats wall reassignment as an explicit step rather than silently re-typing walls
